definitions.explanation: the act of bringing something into a place; often refers to bringing one's own food or drinks to a venue

examples.japanese: {飲食物|いんしょくぶつ}の{持|も}ち{込|こ}みは{禁止|きんし}です。
examples.english: Bringing in food and drinks is prohibited.

examples.japanese: {持|も}ち{込|こ}みOKの{居酒屋|いざかや}を{探|さが}す。
examples.english: I'm looking for an izakaya that allows bringing your own food.

examples.japanese: ワインの{持|も}ち{込|こ}み{料|りょう}は1{本|ほん}1000{円|えん}です。
examples.english: The corkage fee for wine is 1,000 yen per bottle.

notes:
FORMATION:
{持|も}つ (to have/hold) + {込|こ}む (to bring into) → bringing in

COMMON CONTEXTS:
- Restaurants/bars: Bringing own food or alcohol
- Theaters/venues: Bringing food/drinks
- Airports: Bringing items through security
- Hotels: Bringing own bedding, pets, etc.

COMMON SIGNS:
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}み{禁止|きんし} (no outside food/drinks)
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}みOK (bringing in permitted)
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}み{可|か} (bringing in allowed)

RELATED TERMS:
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}み{料|りょう} (corkage/bringing-in fee)
- {飲食|いんしょく}{持|も}ち{込|こ}み (bringing food and drinks)

VERB FORM:
- {持|も}ち{込|こ}む (to bring in)

RELATED:
- {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}り (takeout - opposite direction)
- {差|さ}し{入|い}れ (gift/treat)
- {飲食|いんしょく}{禁止|きんし} (no food or drink)
